confirmed.title: The mako snaps about 90 deg, from side-on to head-on, in two frames
confirmed.evidence: Single-frame crops (shk2.png and shk.png). At f1975 and f1976 the shark is side-on, swimming right across the frame. At f1977 it is rotated about 45 deg. At f1978 it faces the camera head-on and has jumped left. There is no turning arc in between. It happens on the word 'STILL', the payoff of the shark beat. Cause: in sh17b.py, path() ends the arc at u=0.7 with ease() (velocity going to 0) and starts the glide-off at u>0.6 (velocity starting from 0). marine.path_animate orients the shark purely to d = p(f)-p(f-1), so the heading flips to the new (2.2,4.0,-1.2) direction once that term dominates. Banking is smoothed but yaw is not.
confirmed.fix: In sh17b.py, blend the glide-off as a continuation of the arc tangent, for example by starting it earlier with non-zero arc velocity. Alternatively, in lib/marine.py path_animate, smooth the heading by slerping each frame's track quaternion from the previous one with a max yaw of about 6 deg per frame. verdict.reason: I reproduced this with single-frame crops of video frames 1973-1982 (kcstrip.png). Through f1976 the shark is side-on, heading right.
